audit_target: det(I_(m-1)-Q_m) != 0 for T_m = R Bhat R Ahat, where Ahat and Bhat are strictly totally positive Beta-Bernstein moment matrices from the same measure (1-u^(m^2))^(m-1) du, their Bernstein coordinates are linked by u -> u^m, R is the lower binomial Mobius involution, and Q_m is the quotient block after the fixed e_0 direction.

sources.citation: O. Y. Kushel, Cone-theoretic generalization of total positivity, Linear Algebra and its Applications 436(3) (2012), 537-560.
sources.theorem_or_result: GSTP spectral theorem stated in the paper abstract: if every exterior power preserves an appropriate proper cone strictly, the spectrum is positive and simple.
sources.hypotheses: A single linear operator is generalized strictly totally positive with respect to proper cones K_j in every exterior power wedge^j R^n.
sources.mapping: If the full T_m = R Bhat R Ahat can be proved GSTP in a task-specific exterior-cone system, then all eigenvalues of T_m are simple. Since T_m e_0 = e_0, eigenvalue 1 would be simple, which is exactly det(I-Q_m) != 0.
sources.gap: No invariant proper-cone family for the signed Mobius product T_m is currently established. STP of Ahat and Bhat separately does not imply GSTP of R Bhat R Ahat, and the known negative Q_4 entry blocks a direct ordinary-positive-cone argument on Q_m.

sources.citation: Z. Drmac, On Principal Angles between Subspaces of Euclidean Space, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 22(1), 173-194; and H. Klaja, The numerical range and the spectrum of a product of two orthogonal projections, Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 411(1) (2014), 177-195.
sources.theorem_or_result: Principal-angle cosines are the singular values of the cross-Gram matrix Q_X^T Q_Y for orthonormal bases; Klaja Lemma 2.8 gives the spectral interpretation for products of orthogonal projections through the Friedrichs angle.
sources.hypotheses: Two subspaces of one Hilbert space, represented by orthonormal bases / orthogonal projections.
sources.mapping: If T_m (or an eigenvalue-preserving similarity of it) can be realized as a product/compression of two orthogonal projections with the fixed e_0 direction corresponding to their one-dimensional intersection, then eigenvalue 1 has multiplicity exactly the intersection dimension; strict transversality on the quotient would give det(I-Q_m) != 0.
sources.gap: Ahat and Bhat are row-normalized moment transforms, not orthogonal projections; R is a non-orthogonal signed binomial transform. No same-Hilbert-space Gram/projection factorization with one-dimensional intersection has yet been proved.

sources.citation: Bernstein-Jacobi-type operators preserving derivatives, Computational and Applied Mathematics (2024), Section 5 / Corollary 5.1, recovering the classical Durrmeyer-Derriennic and Sablonniere Bernstein-Jacobi spectral theory.
sources.theorem_or_result: Corollary 5.1: Jacobi polynomials are eigenfunctions of the Bernstein-Jacobi operator. Equation (2.5) gives lambda_(n,r) = (n-r+1)_r/(n+alpha+beta+2)_r, with lambda_(n,0)=1 and 0<lambda_(n,r)<1 for 1<=r<=n when alpha,beta>-1.
sources.hypotheses: One Bernstein-Jacobi/Durrmeyer operator built from the same Bernstein basis in input/output with a Jacobi weight x^alpha(1-x)^beta and its associated inner-product normalization.
sources.mapping: This supplies an exact model in which a Beta/Bernstein integral operator has a simple constant fixed point and an explicit spectral gap below 1.
sources.gap: The AP measure rho_m=(1-u^(m^2))^(m-1)du is not a single Jacobi weight in the operative coordinate, the two half maps use Bernstein coordinates u and u^m, and the signed non-orthogonal R is inserted between them. Hence T_m is not identified with this self-adjoint Bernstein-Jacobi operator.

sources.citation: E. E. Berdysheva and K. Jetter, Multivariate Bernstein-Durrmeyer operators with arbitrary weight functions, Journal of Approximation Theory 162(3) (2010), 576-598.
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper develops arbitrary-measure Bernstein-Durrmeyer operators and explicitly notes that, outside the Jacobi setting, degree preservation and orthogonal-polynomial eigenspaces can fail.
sources.hypotheses: Positive regular Borel measure satisfying the paper's positivity assumption; general Bernstein-Durrmeyer kernel.
sources.mapping: The AP weight is naturally compared with this arbitrary-measure extension rather than the Jacobi-special case.
sources.gap: The general-weight theory does not provide the Jacobi spectral diagonalization needed to exclude eigenvalue 1, and the AP operator additionally has the u -> u^m cross-coordinate and R insertions.

sources.citation: S. Cooper and S. Waldron, The Eigenstructure of the Bernstein Operator, Journal of Approximation Theory 105(1) (2000), 133-165.
sources.theorem_or_result: The classical Bernstein operator reproduces all linear polynomials, so eigenvalue 1 is not simple.
sources.mapping: Negative-control analogue for any attempt to infer fixed-point simplicity from Bernstein structure or total positivity alone.
sources.gap: It is not the AP operator; its value is adversarial: it proves that the words 'Bernstein' and 'totally positive' do not by themselves imply a unique fixed vector.

sources.citation: R. Brawer and M. Pirovino, The linear algebra of the Pascal matrix, Linear Algebra and its Applications 174 (1992), 13-23.
sources.theorem_or_result: Classical lower Pascal matrix structure, its factorizations, and inverse/elimination relations.
sources.mapping: For the lower Pascal matrix L_(j,k)=C(j,k), the AP involution R_(j,k)=(-1)^k C(j,k) is a checkerboard/sign variant of binomial inversion (equivalently J L^{-1} under the natural diagonal sign convention). Thus the Mobius factor itself is classical.
sources.gap: The source supplies no theorem about the spectrum of R Bhat R Ahat or its quotient fixed point.

sources.citation: P. Koev and F. Dopico, Accurate eigenvalues of certain sign regular matrices, Linear Algebra and its Applications 424(2-3) (2007), 435-447.
sources.theorem_or_result: Matrices whose kth-order nonzero minors have sign (-1)^(k(k-1)/2) are characterized as nonsingular totally nonnegative matrices with columns in reverse order.
sources.hypotheses: Nonsingular sign-regular matrix with the specified order-dependent minor signature.
sources.mapping: If a signed Mobius-transformed AP half-map acquires this exact minor signature, the result converts it to an ordinary TN structure after column reversal and opens classical oscillation machinery.
sources.gap: This characterization alone gives no eigenvalue-1 exclusion for the normalized product T_m, and no such sign-regularity theorem for the full T_m is frozen in the parent result.

sources.citation: F. R. Gantmacher and M. G. Krein, oscillation-matrix theorem as summarized in Encyclopedia of Mathematics, 'Oscillating matrix'.
sources.theorem_or_result: An oscillatory matrix has n distinct positive eigenvalues and eigenvectors with the classical sign-change pattern.
sources.hypotheses: Totally nonnegative nonsingular matrix with a positive power that is totally positive; equivalent adjacent-entry criteria are available in the classical theorem.
sources.mapping: If an eigenvalue-preserving natural transform of T_m were shown oscillatory, simplicity of its spectrum would immediately exclude a second eigenvalue 1.
sources.gap: Q_4 itself has a proven negative entry, so Q_m is not directly TN in the standard cone. No oscillatory representative of the full Mobius product has been established.

sources.citation: S. Karlin, Total Positivity, Vol. I, Stanford University Press, 1968; basic composition formula and integral-kernel total-positivity framework.
sources.theorem_or_result: Classical basic composition formula: suitable compositions/integrals of totally positive kernels preserve total positivity.
sources.hypotheses: Compatible totally positive kernels and positive measure/integration composition.
sources.mapping: This is a classical antecedent to the Andreief/generalized-Vandermonde mechanism proving Ahat and Bhat STP.
sources.gap: It does not propagate through the signed Mobius involution twice so as to prove fixed-point simplicity of T_m.

required_joint_features: two Bernstein coordinate systems linked by u -> u^m
the row normalizations producing Ahat and Bhat
two insertions of the lower binomial Mobius involution R
